title: Bengaluru Airport Crosses 400 Million Passengers as International Traffic Soars 24%
excerpt: India's third-busiest airport handled 44.47 million travellers in FY26 and won Skytrax's Best Regional Airport for a third straight year — and NRIs are driving the international surge.
body:
Kempegowda International Airport (BLR) has quietly crossed a milestone that took 18 years to reach: 400 million cumulative passengers since it opened in 2008. The achievement, confirmed in BLR's FY2025-26 traffic report, cements Bengaluru's position as one of India's fastest-growing aviation gateways — and a critical artery for the diaspora.

**The numbers behind the milestone**

BLR handled 44.47 million passengers in FY26, a 6.2% year-on-year increase. The real story is international traffic, which surged 23.9% to 7.23 million passengers — comfortably outpacing the 3.3% growth in domestic travel. Cargo hit 532,000 metric tonnes, up 6%, with BLR retaining its crown as India's top perishable export hub. On its busiest single day, the airport processed a record number of passengers that eclipsed anything seen in its history.

**Why international is booming**

The surge reflects a combination of new route launches and pent-up diaspora demand. BLR added direct services to Hanoi, Riyadh, and expanded London frequencies in FY26, bringing its international network to over 33 destinations. IndiGo, Air India, and Cathay Pacific have all ramped capacity on key corridors. The airport's Terminal 2, which opened in 2022, has absorbed much of the growth, with processing times improving even as volumes climb.

**Skytrax recognition cements reputation**

For the third consecutive year, BLR won Skytrax's 'Best Regional Airport in India and South Asia' award — a recognition that reflects both infrastructure investment and operational consistency. COO Girish Nair has emphasised the airport's philosophy of "forward planning over reactive expansion," pointing to technology integration and retail upgrades as differentiators.

**What lies ahead**

BLR's operator, Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), is already planning for the next phase. A third runway, expanded cargo terminals, and deeper technology integration — including biometric processing and AI-driven crowd management — are on the roadmap. With India's aviation market projected to become the world's third-largest by 2030, BLR is positioning itself not just as a domestic hub but as a serious international gateway.

**The diaspora connection**

For the millions of NRIs who fly through Bengaluru each year — visiting family, managing investments, or attending tech conferences — the airport's transformation has been tangible. Shorter immigration queues, more direct international routes, and better retail and lounge options have made the BLR experience markedly different from even five years ago. The 24% international traffic surge is partly a story about airline capacity, but it is equally a story about a diaspora that is flying home more often, on better connections, than ever before.
